task: HDR formalism repair Phase 1, deliverable D (docs/units_convention.md)
specification: Each pair is the cross-lagged fit used by scripts/elsa_lead_lag.py, scripts/inchianti_lead_lag.py and scripts/inchianti_6axis_analysis.py: d_target = beta*source_t0 + gamma*target_t0 + delta*age_t + const, where d_target = x_target(t+1) - x_target(t). Rearranged, x_target(t+1) = (1+gamma)*x_target(t) + beta*x_source(t) + ..., so phi_jj = 1 + gamma and the implied steady-state gain is beta/(1-phi_jj) = -beta/gamma.

units.beta: SD target per SD source per visit interval
units.phi_jj: dimensionless AR(1) coefficient per visit interval
units.long_run_gain: SD target per SD source at steady state
units.interval_years_*: see interval_basis: realised age difference for InCHIANTI, nominal wave-index interval for ELSA

provenance.ELSA: run in-repo from data/elsa/ (UK Data Service SN 5050 extract); nurse-visit waves 2/4/6/8
provenance.InCHIANTI: run against a local copy of the InCHIANTI CD Share; participant-level data was not copied or exported, only these aggregate coefficients
provenance.rounding: InCHIANTI rows are stored to 6 significant figures, so identities such as long_run_gain = beta/(1-phi_jj) hold to ~1e-6 relative on those rows and exactly on ELSA rows.
provenance.note: ELSA nurse-visit waves 2/4/6/8, in-repo data/elsa/; InCHIANTI CD Share, run against a local copy; participant-level data not exported

concordance_definitions.concordant_with_compiled_sign: beta has the sign of the compiled J entry as currently written. Protective F- and B-row entries are negative, so a positive beta counts as discordant under this definition.
concordance_definitions.concordant_all_positive: beta > 0: worse source predicts worse target. The native definition once the protective couplings move to kappa and J is all-positive (docs/protective_coupling_formulation.md).
